references.text: Judas went to the chief priests and the commanders of the temple guard to arrange how he could betray Jesus. Here in verse 52 we see that these very chief priests and temple guards have come to arrest Jesus, fulfilling the plan from verse 4. See [ref:Luk 22:4|Luke 22:4].
The immediate context: Judas came with a crowd to arrest Jesus. In verse 52, Jesus speaks directly to the leaders who accompanied him. See [ref:Luk 22:47-48|Luke 22:47-48].

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says the same words: "Like a robber you have come out with swords and clubs to arrest me." Jesus points out that he sat teaching daily in the temple. See [ref:Matt 26:55|Matthew 26:55].
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus speaks to those who came to arrest him: "Like a robber you have come out with swords and clubs to arrest me." See [ref:Mark 14:48|Mark 14:48].

John's account of the arrest. Judas came with a detachment of soldiers and guards from the chief priests and Pharisees, carrying torches, lanterns, and weapons – precisely the armed force Jesus addresses in Luke 22:52. See [ref:Joh 18:3|John 18:3].

John tells us that the detachment, with its commander and the Jewish guards, arrested Jesus and bound him. The temple guards (στρατηγοί) are mentioned by Luke as part of the arrest force. See [ref:Joh 18:12|John 18:12].

Jesus taught daily in the temple, and the chief priests and scribes sought to have him killed – yet the people clung to him. This is the background for Jesus' argument in verses 52–53: they could have arrested him at any time in the temple. See [ref:Luk 19:47-48|Luke 19:47-48].

Jesus was daily in the temple teaching the people – this supports his point in verse 53 that he was among them in the temple every day without their arresting him. See [ref:Luk 21:37-38|Luke 21:37-38].

Isaiah prophesies about the suffering servant who was oppressed but did not open his mouth, like a lamb led to slaughter. Although Jesus confronts them verbally, he submits to the arrest voluntarily without resistance. See [ref:Jes 53:7-9|Isaiah 53:7-9].

"They hunted me down like a bird, my enemies without cause." The lament describes innocent persecution, reflecting Jesus' words about being treated as a robber without cause. See [ref:Klag 3:52|Lamentations 3:52].

The commanders of the temple guard (στρατηγός τοῦ ἱεροῦ) are also mentioned in Acts when they arrested Peter and John in the temple – the same authority that participated in Jesus' arrest. See [ref:Apg 4:1-3|Acts 4:1-3].
